title: His three favorite trumpeters and losing a job over growling
summary: His favorites were Cootie, Joe Smith and Louis; he was fired by the Irwin Brothers because he could not growl like their coffee-can player Fats.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Well those were my three favorites. Cootie and Joe Smith and Louis.
Yes.
And as I said, the very first trumpet player I liked, I don't know whether I liked him for his playing or what, or how sharp the band was and he had all these horns around him.
Well that's like, I mean that's like kids who go for the trombone because they like the look of that slide.

But I liked this trumpet, but that was way before I ever saw Louis. I used to tell people that he was my favorite trumpet player. Later on, when I started playing myself and getting paid for it, then Louis was first, Cootie second I guess. Because I couldn't growl, like Louis.
I lost a job in California once playing with a band called the Irwin Brothers.
Oh, you skipped them when we were talking, yes.

Irwin Brothers. And they had a boy named Fats that played with a coffee can, just a coffee can, but instead of using a plunger like Cootie did, he used this great big old coffee can, made one noise. And they let him out for some reason and hired me. I couldn't do that so they fired me too.
I could play alright, but I couldn't growl and Fats had been a good growler. So that's the only time I got let out of a job because I couldn't
do something.
Where did you sort of acquire the knowledge of growling?
From different people. There are certain ways to growl. Some people growl with their tongue. And Cootie growls from down in the throat.
So I learned, first I used to growl from the tongue and then I learned how to do it the way Cootie did.
Well you didn't have that much opportunity to do it though did you?

No, no. Well I, you see, when I, I never saw Louis growl so I didn't care about growling. I could play, I could play anything almost if it wasn't too impossible to play that high. I used to play almost anything Louis played and I never growled, I never bothered about growling. Oh, Sweethearts on Parade and those things, it was melody. And even in fast numbers you know, I could hold one note into another. Of course he could hold a note for so long and then, all of that I could do, but I never, Cootie was the only one that I think I growled on something.
I don't remember what it was, but I had a plunger. 2). But you see, Fats couldn't do anything else except growl and he was, that's all he could do.
I think that was the, wasn't that really somewhat the case with Bubber Miley?
Yes, I think so too.
Somebody once said that his open tone was not good.
Yes. So I got canned by them. (LAUGHTER).
